source_profile: US adult women, all ages, all regions. Composition read from the GENDER row across the Gen Pop file and the female cuts of the profile corpus (Reba McEntire - Female, Shark Tank - Female, Protein Enthusiasts - Female, Kardashians - Female), triangulated against the gender splits that platforms and measurement firms publish for their own audiences.
one_line: US adult women, 18 and up, every generation together. About 51 percent of US adults. This lens is not a taste filter: every item stays on the board, and each item is re-valued to the share of its audience that is women, then re-ranked by that number. The job is to get the SHARE right for each item, item by item, from what is known about who actually watches, listens, reads, plays, buys and searches for it.

demographics.age_range: 18 to 80 plus, weighted like the US adult population: roughly a fifth each in 18-29, 30-44, 45-59 and 60 plus, with women outnumbering men above 65.
demographics.gender_skew: 100 percent women by definition. The baseline share of any US audience is about 51 percent; the tilt you return says how far THIS item's audience sits from that baseline.
demographics.income_band: Mirrors the US distribution with a lower median than men (about 82 cents on the dollar in earnings); more single-parent households; more household purchasing decisions (women direct roughly 70 to 80 percent of consumer spending in grocery, health, home and kids).
demographics.education: Women now hold the majority of US bachelor's and graduate degrees among adults under 50; parity or above in every age band under 60.
demographics.occupation_skew: Over-represented in healthcare, education, admin, retail, social services and HR; under-represented in construction, trades, engineering and transport.
demographics.life_stage: Every stage. Mothers of young children are the heaviest users of parenting, kids' streaming and family-film content; women 55 plus are the heaviest cable-news, network-drama, Hallmark, QVC and Costco-app users.
geo_skew: Mirrors the US population. No DMA tilt for the lens as a whole.

values: This is a population, not a subculture. Half of every audience. Do not score women as a niche.

The signal that separates items is COMPOSITION. Romance and romantasy readers are 80 to 90 percent women. Reality TV, daytime, home, cooking, wellness, parenting, beauty, true crime, K-drama, Broadway and lifestyle podcasts run 60 to 80 percent women. Pop, country and Latin pop run 55 to 65 percent women. News, drama, prestige TV, comedy, most streaming top-10s, most search terms and most headlines sit near 50. Sports, action, sci-fi, hip-hop streaming, gaming, crypto, cars, tools and sports-talk run 30 to 45 percent women; hard-core simulation and shooter games, fantasy sports, sports betting and NFL Sunday Ticket run 20 to 35.

Women's share of sports audiences has risen fast where the sport made room for them: WNBA (about 50 percent), women's college basketball, F1 (over 40 percent of new US fans), USWNT and NWSL. Do not apply the 1990s sports default to those.

Women are the majority of the audience for celebrity news, relationship news, royal news, awards shows, and the Kardashian / Real Housewives / Bachelor / Love Is Blind / Love Island / 90 Day universe.
Women are the majority of book buyers overall (about 60 percent), of library borrowers, of audiobook listeners in fiction, and of BookTok.
aesthetics: Not applicable as a taste rule. Read the item for who its audience actually is.
psychographics.tone_they_respond_to: Not a scoring input. This lens measures audience composition, not tone.

themes_they_avoid: Nothing is avoided under this lens. Items simply carry a lower share where the audience is mostly men: fantasy football, sports betting, NFL RedZone, UFC, boxing, motorsport outside F1, sports-talk radio podcasts, shooter and simulation games, crypto and day-trading, cars and tools, men's grooming, most hip-hop deep cuts, hard rock and metal, war and spy thrillers by men, military history, tech-infrastructure headlines.
filter_rules_for_agent: THIS LENS RANKS, IT DOES NOT FILTER. Score is secondary. The TILT is the deliverable: return, for each item, how the women share of ITS audience compares to the 51 percent baseline. tilt 1.0 means 51 percent women. tilt 1.6 means about 82 percent women (romance novels, Bravo, Hallmark). tilt 0.7 means about 36 percent women (NFL game, Call of Duty, sports-talk podcast). tilt 0.45 means about 23 percent women (fantasy football, UFC, Madden).

Anchor on published audience composition wherever it is known: Nielsen and network sales decks for TV, Edison and Spotify for podcasts and music, Circana and BookScan for books, ESA and Newzoo for games, Pew and Statista for platforms and search. When unknown, reason from the closest known comparable, not from a stereotype about the topic.

Streaming top-10 titles mostly sit between 0.85 and 1.25. Push above 1.3 only for romance, reality-dating, K-drama, Hallmark, Bridgerton-class and family-with-mom-decides titles. Push below 0.8 only for sports, action franchises with a male lead and no romance line, war, sci-fi and hard sci-fi, most anime shonen.

Never return the same tilt for a whole panel. Two titles on one chart with different audiences must carry different tilts. Keep the fourth decimal alive.
Score (0-100) should still be filled and should track the tilt: a tilt of 1.5 reads as 85 to 95, 1.0 as 50 to 60, 0.5 as 15 to 25. It is only used for tooltips and cutoffs in other modes.
expected_kept_share_per_tab: 100 percent of items on every tab. This lens runs in rank mode: nothing is hidden, every row is re-valued to its women audience and re-ordered.

reasoned_from_profile.profile_key: Gen_Pop_2026.csv GENDER row (women 51.1) and the female cuts of the profile corpus, read against published audience gender splits.
reasoned_from_profile.note: The lens exists so a reader can sort any board by its women audience. It is a composition read, not a persona brief; the tilt bands above are the calibration and the per-item reasoning is what moves an item off its band.
